prompt: Thin a list out by deleting every nth item. Complete removeEveryNth so it edits the list in place and returns how many items it removed.
explanation: Removing from a list while walking forwards shifts every later element down one slot, so the positions you still want to delete move out from under you. Walking backwards avoids the problem entirely: indexes you have not visited yet are never disturbed. The guard for n < 1 also protects the % operator from a division by zero when n is 0.
hints: Positions are counted 1-based, so the element at index i sits at position i + 1 -- it should go when (i + 1) % n == 0.
Loop from the END of the list back to the start so removing an element cannot shift the items you have not checked yet.
Handle n < 1 before the loop: it removes nothing, and it would also make the % operator blow up when n is 0.
